symptom: Changes to spending source paths did not select the registered spending walkthroughs, and nightly exit 125 was reported as a failure.
direct_cause: The walk list was copied into validation policy and workflow YAML, while the nightly summary used status !== 0 for failures.
class_root: There was no single executable routing contract shared by source-path classification, blocking PR execution, nightly execution, and result aggregation.
internal_only_reason: The invariant is repository-specific CI routing and does not depend on a third-party runtime contract.
invariants: The routing table is the only owner of spending walkthrough membership and blocking status.
Every spending source path and registered spending walk selects the journey lane.
Exit 125 is skipped; only nonzero statuses other than 125 are failures.
Every walk has a bounded timeout and browser provisioning uses the shared retrying script.

door_reduction.why_not: These four consumers intentionally remain separate execution doors, but all read the same routing contract or its executable CLI output.

generality_proof: Policy, PR workflow, nightly workflow, and summary code all consume the same routing JSON or the same summary function, so adding or changing a walk cannot leave one execution surface stale.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Own the complete walk set, blocking subset, and rationale.
Route source paths and registered walks to the journey lane and expose the executable blocking list.
Classify pass, skipped, timeout, and failure statuses consistently.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Runs every non-paid walk with the shared browser installer and per-walk timeout.
Regression test proves status 125 is skipped and 124 is failed.

recurrence.reason: Any newly added spending source, walk, runner status, or workflow edit could otherwise drift from the other surfaces.
same_class_scan: rg spending path rules and walk names across scripts, workflows, and tests

prevention.invariant: All spend routing and blocking selection is derived from test-routing.json.
prevention.failure_mode: Missing spend-walks data throws during policy load; unknown paths remain fail-closed under existing policy rules.
prevention.strategy: Remove copied lists from workflow YAML and make summary status semantics executable and tested.

legacy_paths.rationale: Copied routing and inline status classification were replaced by shared data and executable helpers.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No third-party dependency controls the routing invariant.

migration: No persisted user data or production API changes; existing workflows consume the new routing entry on their next run.
residual_risks: Actual Linux Electron walkthrough execution remains unverified in this local Windows session and is delegated to CI/nightly evidence.
